This mythological figure was able to conquer Megara after earning the love of Scylla, who betrayed her father, the Megaran King Nisus, by cutting off Nisus's purple hair, making the city vulnerable to this man's attack. After his death by scalding at the hands of the daughters of Cocalus, this man served as a judge of the dead with Aeacus and Rhadamanthys. His son Androgeos was killed after winning a number of athletic contests in another city, leading this man to exact a cruel tribute from the city every nine years, insisting that seven young men and seven young women be sent to be killed by the offspring of this man's wife Pasiphae. FTP who was this Cretan king who had Daedalus build the Labyrinth to house the Minotaur?

One of this deity's offspring killed Nanaki, a sacred pheasant, with an arrow, which this deity promptly threw back down to earth, killing him. The largest shrine to this deity is torn down and rebuilt every 20 years, and its interior is thought to house the "eight-hand mirror," sacred to this deity. Born when her father washed his left eye, this creator of the "inada," or fields of rice, was tricked by the dancing Ame-no-Uzume into leaving a cave into which she had fled after being offended by the flayed horse thrown at her by her brother Susanoo. FTP name this kami, the Shinto sun goddess.

Dr. Valentine McGillicuddy and John Gregory Bourke disagree over whether a guard's bayonet or his own knife killed this individual, and Touch the Clouds saved this man from assassination by No Water. A witness of the Grattan Massacre, this man initiated the Fetterman Massacre, and suffered losses at Slim Buttes and Wolf Mountain before surrendering at Camp Robinson, Nebraska. Victor of the Battle of the Rosebud, which prevented George Crook from bringing his troops to aid George Custer against this man and Chief Gall at Little Bighorn, name this Oglala Sioux war hero who fought alongside Red Cloud and Sitting Bull.

Later in his life this figure's intended bride Grainne ran off with Diarmuid who would join him in a boar hunt and get badly gored. He would later fail to save Diarmuid's life by letting water intended for Diarmuid slip through his fingers for water drunk from his hands had healing powers. Among his other powers was that while sucking his thumb he could summon wisdom from a burn he received while cooking for Finnegas. Name this hero of Irish myth who will wake from his cave below Dublin to save Ireland in her direst hour and tasted of the Salmon of Knowledge.

This figure considered a giant thermocouple impractical for powering his Krupp engines, using sodium-mercury batteries instead. This descendant of Sultan Tipu of Mysore is revealed to Cyrus Smith on his deathbed as the genie of Lincoln Island, years after he claimed the South Pole with a black flag. Exiled after his leadership in the Sepoy Rebellion and thereafter operating under a pseudonym also used by Odysseus, this polyglot's lasting hatred for Britain leads to his declaring "I am the law! I am justice!" and ramming a frigate before turning his own vessel toward the Maelstrom. Born Prince Dakkar, what name meaning "nobody" was used by the captain of the Nautilus created by Jules Verne?

This Olympian goddess was the mother of the super-fast horse Arion, whom she bore after being raped by Poseidon in horse form. While on a search, she was hospitably received by the king Celeus, whose son Triptolemus she trained in the skill she represented as goddess. At Tantalus's banquet, she accidentally ate the shoulder of Pelops, whom she later brought back to life. The most famous story involving her is the likely basis of the Eleusinian Mysteries. FTP who is this Greek deity whose daughter Persephone was taken from her by Hades, the goddess of agriculture?

One offspring of this deity was the murderous Kyknos, who was building a temple from the bones of his victims before being killed by Heracles. In Sparta, youths would sacrifice puppies to this god, and a statue of him in chains stood just east of Sparta. When Cadmus killed a dragon guarding a spring sacred to this deity, he had to work for him for eight years, though Cadmus did get to marry this god's daughter Harmonia. His sister was the personification of discord, Eris, and his sons were Phobos and Deimos. Name this Greek war god.

In Batryomyomachia, Homer's description of the war between frogs and mice, Zeus sends an army of these creatures to drive off the victorious mice at the end. The Heikegani are types of these creatures said in Japan's Tale of Heike to be the spirits of defeated samurai, the faces of which can be seen in the carapace of these creatures. Carcinos was a giant one which was crushed while attempting to help the Hydra defeat Heracles, and for his efforts was placed in the sky by Hera. FTP what is this littoral crustacean that is represented as the fourth Zodiacal sign, Cancer?

As a result of the churning of the ocean, this god acquired a white horse. The spirits known as the Asparas would dance for this god in Svarga, which was located on Mount Meru. This leader of the Devas absorbed many of Varuna's functions, and his assisstants were the Maruts [muh-ROOTS], who used axes to split the clouds in order to make it rain. In addition to Agni, this god drank a lot of soma, and he was the father of Arjuna. In order to slay his enemies or revive those killed in battle, he carries the thunderbolt Vajra. This god rode the white elephant Airavata, and killed the water-stealing serpent-demon Vritra. FTP name this Vedic god.

One of this person's adversaries tells him that he will "let cawing buzzard, screaming eagle, and vulture feed on [his] flesh" and claims his companion "not know his father." Inadvertant creator of the Lrbanon rift valley, this man enlists Shamash's aid to reach a cedar tree, which required defeating Humbaba. His companion was originally a wild man created to distract him from his tyrannical rule, but they become fast friends until the latter kills the Bull of Heaven and is struck down by Ishtar. Identify this two-thirds-immortal friend of Enkidu; a Sumerian hero who sought immortality in the oldest extant epic.

This figure's doctor mixed placebos into his stash of sleeping pills to try to cure his addiction and also reported that this man had once believed his swimming pool to be poisoned. Surviving the disgrace of Otto Braun and the execution of his first wife in 1930, he followed the tactics of Zhu De to gain the leadership of the group with which he is most associated at the Zunyi conference before reaching Yan'an. Identify this man who completed the Long March to lead the Chinese Communist Party to victory.

These creatures uniquely possess ten sex chromosomes, one of which is the ZZ/ZW pattern that they share with birds. Venom from these animals' crural glands can lead to oedema and hyperalglesia, though they do not use their vemom for hunting, instead using electroreceptors that detect the muscle contractions of their prey as they move through water. Not found on New Guinea, these creatures join echidnas to comprise order monotremata. Name these amphibious Australian mammals.

This being's spittle is the source of the river Van or Hope, which emanates from Gioll, a rock. The father of Hati and Skoll, harassers of the moon and sun, this creature is the eldest child of Angrboda and Loki. Gleipnir was attached to this beast when Tyr sacrificed a hand. Name this devourer of Odin, a fearsome wolf of Norse myth.

According to the Catalogues of Women, this man's father was cursed by Zeus and could never have children of his own, so he was a son of Poseidon by Eurynome. After he journeyed from Ephyra to Tiryns, Stheneboea attempted to seduce him, which lead to a second exile, but she would kill herself after learning of his marriage to her sister Philonoe. He was given Philonoe's hade after defeating the Solymi, the Amazons, and the Chimera. Identify this man who achieved those feats with the help of the horse Pegasus.

According to the 33rd of Parthenius' Love Stories, this mythological figure fell in love with his daughter, then burned her children to death. His grandson of the same name was King of Pisa killed by Agamemnon. This ruler of Mount Sipylus was once crushed under a rock for lying about knowing the location of a golden dog made by Hephaestus. One of his sons was driven mad by Artmeis and threw himself upon a lighted pyre and another had his left shoulder eaten by Demeter. Name this father of Broteas, Niobe, and Pelops, who was eternally tempted with food and water in Tartarus.

The Scottish water devil Kelpie assumes the shape of one of these animals to trick travelers. In Korean myth, one of these animals bowed to a shining egg that contained the first king of Shilla. In Irish myth, Niamh owned one of these animals that could travel over waves. In Norse myth, a frost giant offered to rebuild the walls of Asgard with the help of one of these named Svadilfari, the mother of an even more famous one with eight legs. In Greek myth, one created from the blood of Medusa had wings. Name this animal, the most famous of which include Sleipnir and Pegasus.

This figure's children include Golgos and Beroe. Daedalus presented a honeycomb to he at shrine at Eryx, and she slept with Butes at Lilybaeum. Born to Dione at Paphos, she castrated Attis and caused the daughter of Phoenix, Smyrna, to procreate with her father, resulting in a child born from a myrrh tree. She also gave birth to Rhodus and Herophilus for Poseidon and produced an androgynous being for Hermes. When her husband was supposed to be on holiday on Lemnos, she got trapped in a net with Ares. Name this Greek deity born from the foam of the sea, the goddess of desire and love.

This person's Tolstoy farm settlement was inspired by a reading of The Kingdom of God Is Within You. His truce with Lord Irwin led to the Round Table conference and he returned to politics after criticizing Sir John Simon's reform commission. Residing late in his life at Sevagaram, he earlier practiced law at Natal, South Africa, where he developed the satyagraha movement, which he later applied to protest the salt tax. Name this man murdered by a Hindu fanatic, the father of India, called a mahatma.

He spared Aífe on the requirement that she bear him a son and stop fighting his teacher Scáthach. He was immune to the curse of Macha and had seven toes, fingers, and eyes. He met his end, however when he fell under the illusion of battle by six sorcerers sent by Maeve, the queen of Connacht. This animosity grew out of his opposition to Maeve during the Cattle Raid of Cooley. Identify this hero of the Ulster Cycle, wielder of the spear Gae Bolg whose name comes from his killing of a smith's dog.

According to Euripides's Andromache, he slew Achilles's son Neoptolemus over the latter's wife, Hermione. Throughout the Odyssey, he is held up as an example for Telemachos to follow, but in a namesake play, he is criticized by Tyndareus for his most famous action. Despite the efforts of his friend Pylades, that action eventually leads him to be driven mad and to be pursued by the Furies all the way to Athens. Name this son of Agamemnon, who avenges his father's death by murdering Aegisthus and his lover, this man's mother.

Kennings that dub the sky a "thing of" this god mean that he may be more similar to Zeus and Jupiter than another god he is more commonly associated with. His consort is identified as Zisa in a very early text, and in the Lokasenna, Loki threatens to cuckold this god. His rune is an arrow pointing upwards, and he was known as the god of temples. At Ragnarok, he is destined to be killed by the dog that guarded the gates of Hel, Garm. The most famous story about him concerns how, upon being bound with Gleipnir, Fenrir bit off his right hand. Identify this Norse god of combat, the namesake of Tuesday.

One item by this name is stolen by Nasir and given to Ena, eventually making its way to Ashnard. That artifact, also known as Lehran's Medallion, is carried by Mist, and another artifact by this name is the Stone of Rausten, which was used to seal away the Demon King by twin monarchs of Renais, Ephraim and Eirika. Yet another artifact by this name is used to anoint the monarch of Bern, and must be retrieved by Eliwood long before it is used to unlock the Sword of Seals. Give the common name of this artifact, which in one instance was retrieved by Ike, and gives its name to the series of games starring Roy and Marth.

Krishna was given the gem Syamantaka by the Hindu king of these animals, Jambavantha. Agrius and Oreus were half-human and half this creature before they were turned into birds, and another Greek myth has it that Atalanta was raised by one after being abandoned in the forest. Korean legend states that Tangun, founder of the nation, was born from a woman who had previously been one of these animals. The daughter of Lycaon was turned into one of these animals after Zeus raped her and impregnated her with Arcas, who later almost killed her while hunting. What is this animal into which the nymph Callisto was changed, and is represented in the stars by Ursa Major.

One analogue of this character wins a wrestling match with an earthquake god to retain the right to cook. Another story has him gaining an epithet when his mother throws him into the water wrapped in her hair; he later follows that mother to the underworld as a wood pigeon. He dealt with people's complaints about the length of the day by gathering his brothers, snaring the Sun, and beating it with a jawbone until it slowed down. That jawbone was also used as a hook by this character to pull up the earth's land, including the islands of New Zealand. Name this Polynesian and Maori trickster god.

One of them holds a mace that represents knowledge; that one also bore a mountain on his back on which the gods rode. One of them defeated the demon Goldeneye to recover the Earth from the bottom of the cosmic ocean, while another avoided a boon given to the father of a devotee by jumping out of a pillar. The axe-wielding one will train the one that will appear riding a winged horse to end the Kali Yuga, and they include a fish, a tortoise, and a boar. Give the name for this group of figures including Matsya, Kurma, Varaha, Parashurama, Krishna, and Buddha, the earthly representations of a certain Hindu preserver god.

FIST Editors Packet #1 In one story, this figure is sent to the island of Fuarfed to aid the king Malorchol in battle against Tonthormod, while in another he is driven to set sail after dreaming of the shadow of Trenmor. He wins three games of chess when Diarmuid helps him by dropping berries on the piece he's supposed to move. He relates that he came to the aid of Crothar, the king of Croma, to console the lover of his deceased son Malvina. He is given the horse Embarr, but when its golden saddle breaks, the fact that this figure had spent the last 300 years in Tir-na Nog with his lover Niamh causes him to turn into an old man upon touching the mortal soil of Ireland. His name stems from his mother Sedb being turned into a deer. FTP, name this father of Oscar and son of Finn MacCool, a famous poet in Celtic myth.

One of this god's sons was kept a secret by enclosing him in a box and sending him down the Asva River, but he was pulled out by Adhiratha who raised him with his wife Radha. That son was born when Kunti summoned this god using a mantra of Durvasa, only to discover that she'd obliged herself to have a virgin birth. This god's wife escaped him by creating a shadow of herself named Chaya, which bore him children like Tapati. When he found that Chaya was not his true wife, this god took the form of a stallion and seduced his wife in the forest to produce Nasatya and Dasra, also known as the Aswin twins. This god is commonly cited as a member of the first Vedic triad along with Indra and Agni, and he's often depicted with seven horses and Aruna, who drives his one-wheeled chariot. FTP, name this ancient Hindu god of the sun.

Mention] One resident of this location was a prophet named Abaris who possessed a magical arrow that allowed him to fly, while other residents included five men known as the Perpherees who were kidnapped, after which residents of this place refused to deliver gifts in person. It was also home to three handmaidens named Hecaerge, Loxo, and Upis and three giant sons of Khione. One story holds that, in imitation of Kyknos, the residents of this place leap into a lake to turn themselves into singing swans, though swans are mute beyond its borders. This location is home to the Eridanos river and is accessed by crossing the Rhipaion mountains, from which its namesake deity is said to swoop. The three nymphs of this place introduced the worship of Apollo to Delos, since Apollo is the only god worshipped here, and all residents are his servant. FTP, name this blessed land of eternal sunshine located beyond the land of the griffins, so named because it is also beyond the North Wind.

One interpretation of a myth says that this deity performed self-sacrifice, along with Tecciztecatl and Nanahuatzin, to create the sun. Another myth states that this deity was involved in the creation of the wind deity Ehecatl, who is usually an aspect of one of this god's children. This deity was the subject of a murder plot by Coyolxauqui who rallied the "four hundred southerners" into a mass beheading, until another deity sprang into life fully armed and slew them. Known for wearing a necklace of hearst, ahnds, and skulls and a skirt of writhing snakes, she was impregnated by a ball of feathers while sweeping a temple, leading her to birth twins. FTP, name this mother of Xolotl, Huitzlipoctli, and Quetzalcoatl, the Great Mother goddess of Aztec mythology.

In one myth, this figure eases the labor pains of the Maid-of-the-Moon, or the "Cow of Sin," by employing his daughter, a demon named Lamashtu. He was said to have created the brick god Kullu and he is the father of seven demons called the Utukki. In another story, this figure denies immortality to Adapa, after he refuses the food of life offered by this deity. The special stones of this god were objects of Gilgamesh's misplaced affections in dreams which portended the coming of Enkidu. In Hurrian tradition, this deity's son Kummarbi bites off his penis, and is impregnated as a result of that act. In Babylonian myth, this son of Anshar and Kishar is often said to send the Bull of Heaven against Gilgamesh on behalf of his daughter Ishtar. FTP, name this member of a triad with Enlil and Ea, the Mesopotamian god of the sky.

According to the Bundahishn, this figure slays the primal creature from whose seed all animals emerge and is subdued by the chanting of the Ahuna Vairya. This being supposedly created Jeh the Whore, who afflicts women with menstruation. He rips open his mother's womb to claim lordship over the world, but his rule is then limited to a mere nine thousand years. This deity subsequently suffers a stupor that lasts three thousand years, and allies with the Daevas against the Yazatas in a struggle that he will eventually lose to his good twin. Identify this Zoroastrian deity, the evil counterpart to Ahura Mazda.

This figure is sometimes said to be the half-brother of Coronis, the mother of Asclepius. His refusal to pay a bridal price for Dia caused Deioneus, his father-in-law, to steal some of his horses. When this man found out, he took revenge by inviting Deioneus to a feast, and then pushing him into a fire. His neighbors ostracized him for his betrayal, causing him to go mad. Zeus took pity and invited him to Olympus, where he tried to rape Hera. Zeus found out about his intentions and made a cloud called Nephele in the shape of Hera, which he raped. Zeus then punished him by having Hermes bind him to a wheel of fire. Name this mythical king of the Lapiths.

One myth says that this goddess is the mother of adeity who cuts down trees during the day that are set up again at night by fairies. This goddess had a little sister who took the form of an egg, and was mysteriously transformed into a young girl after being held in this goddess's skirt. Her brother, the king of dragons and sharks, sent all her siblings to join this goddess after she found the the Navel of the World. Ocean craters are believed to be the remnants of her abandoned attempts to dig foundations for houses after she was exiled by Kane Milohai. Name this goddess who lives in the Kilauea volcano and creates eruptions and fire in Hawaiian myth.

This man made a case study of a young girl who dreamed that the world was swallowed by a sea-serpent but saved by a Christlike figure. In that book, this man wrote of such examples of a title concept as the round flat stone, the red-eyed devil, and the divine quaternity. This author of "Memories, Dreams, and Reflections," "Interpretation of Nature and Psyche," "Synchronicity and Christhood," and "Psychology of Religion" used the afore- described work, Man and His Symbols, to outline his theory of archetypes, animus and anima, and the collective unconscious. Name this author of Psychological Types, a Swiss associate of Freud.

He is the god associated with the Mazatl, or deer, day sign in the Codex Borgia, as well as with the diseases of dropsy and rheumatism. His father was occasionally said to be the moon god Tecciztecatl, while his consort was known as "She Who Wears a Jade Skirt", Chalchiuhtlicue. He was commonly depicted as blue with a mask or rings around his eyes, and during the sixth month of the year, his priests shook "fog rattles" and bathed in the lake to appease him. Name this counterpart to the Mayan Chac, an Aztec god of water and rain.

In a Slavic folktale, a peahen turns into a princess so her sisters can still these items, while in Romanian myth they are fought over by the zmeu and Praslea the Brave. Three of these were changed into lions by Hera out of spite when either Melanion or Hippomenes forgot to thank her for their use in defeating his beloved. Ladon was sent to guard them by Hera, but Atlas was tricked into acquiring them from him, though Athena had Heracles return them to the Hesperides. Freia's provide eternal youth, but the most famous of them was owned by Eris, who threw it on the ground at the wedding of Peleus and Thetis, which caused a beauty pageant to break out under the judgment of Paris. Name this discordant fruit that caused the Trojan War.

Viktor Rydberg proposed in the book Teutonic Mythology that this creature may be the same character as Gullveig, a mysterious woman in the Voluspa who is burned and reborn three times in Odin's hall. She is also usually identifed with the "woman of the iron wood" in the Prose Edda. According to the Voluspa, this being lived in Jarnvior. Her heart was ultimately eaten by one god, leading to the birth of a figure who is half black and half white. She gave birth to Skoll and Hati by a lupine partner, and Loki coupled with her to produce the ruler of Helheim. Name this mother of the Midgard Serpent and Fenrir.

In Shinto myth, the kami of this subdued Kagase-wo the Star-God. One figure who performs this action appeared to Gou Zi-Yi and told him that he was the god of wealth; that figure is referred to as the "Heavenly" one. Frigg performs this action in order to create the clouds, and in Greek mythology, one group that performed this action got drunk at the behest of Apollo, thus sparing Admetus' life. Another person who performed this action angered a deity by depicting the gods' faults, leading to her being turned into a spider. Name this action performed by Clotho, Atropos, and Lachesis, as well as during a contest between Athena and Arachne.

Kusku attempted to resurrect this god's son by submerging him in a lake, while another death-related myth claims that in his haste to see his dead wife he opened a box containing dead souls before he had reached the land of the living. Another myth attributes the creation of the horse to him, and he defeated the testicle-eating Moon and created a new man from Moon's blood in one creation myth. Sometimes depicted as an old man who passes on knowledge of the sacred rites, he stole fire from the Fire Beings and allegedly spied on Badger and other animals while impersonating the moon. Name this trickster deity of the American Southwest.

His father torched Apollo's temple at Delphi after Apollo seduced his sister Coronis, leading to the birth of the great healer Asclepius. According to the Iliad, his wife Dia was seduced by Zeus, a union that created Pirithous, although this man is more often considered Pirithous' father. He was the first to shed kindred blood when he killed his father-in-law with burning coals, but when Zeus purified him and invited him to Olympus, this man proved he was not quite as skilled at seduction. In an attempt to seduce Hera, he ended up impregnating a cloud to become the ancestor of the Centaurs. Name this man who, in punishment, remains bound to a fiery wheel in Tartarus.

This man's first wife shares her name with a daughter of Erechtheus who was the mother of Achaeus and Ion. His father was a son of Capys who traveled with Antenor on a failed mission to ransom Hesione. This man rescues Achaemenides while leading a band that includes Palinurus and the faithful Achates. He defeats king Mezentius after allying with king Evander, and he avenges the death of Evander's son Pallas by killing a prince of the Rutuli. After losing his first wife, Creusa, he marries the daughter of Amata and Latinus, Lavinia. FTP, name this son of Anchises whose adventures following the Trojan War were recounted in a namesake epic poem written by Virgil.

According to the Prose Edda, a kenning for sword is "head of" this god who was also known as the Golden-Toothed or Wind-Shelter. He slept with such women as Edda and Amma as Rig, the father of mankind. Rather confusingly, he is the son of nine maidens, who are also his sisters. He rides the mount Gulltopr and has the hall Himinbjorg but he may be better known for being able to hear the grass grow. He will fight Loki to the death at Ragnarok, which he will call to gods to battle with the Gjallarhorn. FTP, identify this watchman of the gods who guards the bridge Bifrost.

This god was believed to influence the destiny of the artisans in the Deir-el-Medina district of the city he is most associated with. The similarity of this god's name to a Semitic root meaning "to open" indicates he may have once been a fertility god. As Ta-Tenen, this god "gave birth to the gods". He also exists as the primeval waters, Nun, and he is often associated with Sokar and Osiris. Identify this chief god of Memphis.

Under the guise of Vegtam, Odin consulted with the dead prophetess Vala about this other god's fate. This god's son lives in the hall Glitnir. The insolent dwarf Littur was kicked onto this man's ship, Ringhorn, during a ceremony that also saw Odin give this god the ring Draupnir and whisper unknown words into his ear. Hermod's attempts to plead for his return were foiled by the giantess Thokk, who refused to cry over his death. Name this husband of Nanna, the Norse god of joy and beauty, felled by a sprig of mistletoe thrown by his brother Hodur under Loki's treacherous aim.

He fathered the god of fishermen without incident, but his wife died while giving birth to the god of fire. In a story mirroring the Orpheus myth, he goes down to the underworld to retrieve his wife, but when he looks back at his wife, she is already rotting and maggot-ridden, and he is disgusted by the sight. Afterwards, he cleanses himself, creating the sun from his left eye and the moon from his right. He had created the world, along with his companion, by plunging a jewel-studded spear into the ocean, a drop from which formed the first island of Japan. FTP, name this Shinto god of the primordial sky, the husband and brother of Izanami.

This man fathered the winner of a footrace at the Nemean Games, Melanippus, with Perigune, who had just witnessed this man kill her father. He slew all fifty Pallantids as well as Pallas himself to secure his position as heir to his father's throne, and he defeated Creon to allow Adrastus to bury the fallen Argives after the Seven Against Thebes had been turned back. This man lifted a gigantic rock to reveal his father's sword and sandals. Two other sons of this man, Acamas and Demophon, were conceived with a wife who hanged himself after his son by another woman rejected her advances. FTP, name this Athenian hero best known for killing the Minotaur.

This goddess convinced one of her lovers to attempt to seduce his wife while in disguise; after he became convinced of his wife's infidelity, she whisked him off to Syria. After finding out about this goddess's affair with Ares, Aphrodite cursed this daughter of Hyperion and Theia to remain perpetually in love, and among her other lovers were Astraeus and Orion. She requested to Zeus that another of her lovers be made immortal but, since she forgot to ask also for eternal youth, he grew older and older until he eventually withered into a cricket. Name this lover of Tithonus, a goddess who opens the gates of heaven every day so that her brother Helios can ride his chariot across the sky.

The Golden Bough notes that "at Braunrode, in the Harz Mountains", these creatures were customarily burned in the Easter bonfire. In the Kalevala, a white one born of a virgin is charged with retrieving beer-making items from the "woods of watchful Tapio". In India, the stripes on their backs are considered to be the mark of Rama's fingers. Another of these creatures carries insults between Vedrfolnir and Nidhogg while running up and down Yggdrasil. Identify this rodent whose most mythologically well-known member may be Ratatosk.

The Columbus, Ohio zoo was the first to breed these creatures in captivity, and the first to be born in the zoo was thus named "Colo". These animals are prone to the heart disease Cardiomyopathy, and recently zoos have begun giving pacemakers to some of these. One species of this animal lives exclusively in the Albertine rift forests. Apart from the Mountain variety of these, two other species are the Western and Eastern lowland. Adult males of this animal are termed "silverbacks", and this animal demonstrates dominance by beating its chest. These animals can learn sign language and adopt kittens, as shown by Koko. Name this largest of the great apes, the second closest relative to humans after chimps.

In the full title of an Egyptian pharaoh, the sedge plant represented Upper Egypt, with this creature representing Lower Egypt. Because of a belief that these animals were symbols of the Merogivgian dynasty, Napoleon gave himself an imperial coat of arms that contained these creatures and their dwelling. In one book about these creatures, they work hard to supply each other's lust and vanity, then are granted virtue by God and see their society collapse. That book was subtitled "Private Vices, Public Virtues", was by Bernard Mandeville, and is called the "Fable of" these creatures. Name these members of Hymenoptera, social insects that fly, sting, and make honey.

In Hindu myth, the legendary King Shibi proved his generosity by offering to let himself get eaten by one of these creatures. An Egyptian god with the head of this animal was associated with the "hennu boat"; that god was an early funerary deity from Memphis named Sokar. According to Snorri's Gylfaginning, Habrok is the best of these creatures. Another animal of this kind from Norse myth is Vedrfolnir, who sits between the eyes of a related species on top of Yggdrasil. Name this bird of prey smaller than an eagle.

Archaeoindris, which went extinct 2,000 years ago, was the largest known of these creatures to ever live and weighed up to 500 pounds. The large and slow "sloth" variety of this animal also went extinct upon contact with humans. The Sifaka and the Indri are the largest living species of these creatures. These creatures have an elongated claw on their second finger, which they use for grooming and cleanliness and which is called the "toilet- claw". Notable species of these creatures include the Loris and the Eye- Eye, as well as the iconic Ring-tailed. All living species are found on Madagascar. Name these basal primates, which according to a popular expression are " Leapin' ".

This creature was voiced by Burgress Meredith in animated films which saw him visit the "Land of the Living Lies" and meet the "Incredible Mr. Nobody". This creature first appeared in a poem written by a 19-year old Cornell student who would later write the lyrics to Madonna's "Like a Virgin", Lenny Lipton. This creature is given strings and ceiling wax as gifts and his roar would make pirate ships lower their flags. This creature from Honalee had a notable friendship with little Jackie Paper, a boy who eventually stops visiting him. Name this titular creature of a Peter, Paul, and Mary song.

According to Wikipedia, this creature was depicted on the helmet of the mythical Swedish king Ali, also called Onela, and after Ali's defeat in battle that helmet was used by the mythical Swedish king Adlis, who is mentioned in Beowulf as having a helmet with the kind of animal that this creature is. During a trip to visit the prophetic giantess Hyndla, the pious man Ottar is disguised as this creature. This creature's owner also owns a magic falcon- feather cloak and Brisingamen, a necklace. This creature is sometimes used in place of a chariot pulled by gib-cats. Name this boar belonging to the Norse Goddess Freya.

They're not penguins, but the Indian Runner breed of this animal waddles. The dabbling variety of these members of Anatidae eat off the surface of water; that group includes the Australasian and Cape Shovelers. Amusingly named species of these birds include the Bufflehead. The breed of this bird most commonly eaten by Americans, such as the villainous Susan Ferrari, is the Pekin or Long Island, which is domesticated. A highly ornamental species of this is the "Wood" one, while the most common American species of this bird has males with a bright green head, known as a mallard. Name this bird that goes quack.

This creature guards Svarga, a place where righteous souls go before being reincarnated. This creature's mother was Iravati, and this creature was born after hymns were sung over the egg from which Garuda hatched. This creature was once depicted on the flags of Laos and Siam. This creature is depicted with either three or five heads and with pure white skin. The owner of this creature uses the vajra weapon, slays the serpent Vritra, and is the god of thunder. Name this elephant from Hindu myth, the mount of Indra.

According to one description, this creature's eyes were red like cherries, and fir and cyprus trees were growing on its back. This creature lived near the Hi River, and it demanded human sacrifice once a year for seven years. Fences and gates were constructed as part of a plot to have this creature drink liquor, after which it passed out and was slain. This figure's killer had transformed his future wife into a comb to protect her from this creature. This creature had eight tails and eight heads and its body contained the sword Kusanagi. Name this serpent from Japanese myth, slain by Susanowo.

This animal's second-to-last owner was a brother of Sarpedon, while it's first mortal owner was a daughter of Agenor who received this creature from Zeus. One owner of this creature gave this creature and a javelin away as a gift after being cured of a condition in which he ejaculated spiders and scorpions. That owner, who later became a judge of the dead, was King Minos of Crete. This animal's doom was caused by Cephalus, a hunter who was married to this animal's last owner, Procris. This animal was turned to stone by Zeus after being sent after the Teumessian fox, which could never be caught, thus preventing a paradox. Name this dog from Greek mythology that would always catch what it chased.

This creature was depicted at the feet of the namesake enthroned god at the Serapeum temple in Alexandria. In Ovid's Metamorphoses, this creature is called "Medusaeum". This creature had a similar-looking sibling named Orthrus. A cavern on the peninsula of Tainaron was once used to find this creature. This creature's mane was made of snakes, and it also had a serpentine tail. The Sibyl in the Aeneid fed this creature a cake, and this creature was captured for Eurystheus as the twelfth and final labor of Hercules. Name this three-headed dog from Greek myth.

In one movie, this creature is killed by time travelers during World War Two, only to be reborn when a Russian submarine sinks in the present, while in another movie this creature has a son named Minya. The MOGUERA robot and the Super-X plane were designed to defeat this creature, which was first killed by using an "Oxygen Destroyer". In one movie, this creature teamed up with the robot Jet Jaguar to defeat the god of Seatopia, Megalon. Enemies of this creature include Anguirus, Gigan, and a three-headed golden dragon, Ghidorah. This creature can light up the spikes on its back and breath a blue radioactive ray, which it used to kill Mothra. Name this giant radioactive dinosaur from Japanese cinema.

The burrows dug by this creature are called "setts". The Philippine island of Palawan is home to the "stink" variety of this creature. Africa is home to a creature called the Ratel, which is called the "honey" variety of this. Dogs bred to hunt this creature include the Daschund, better known as the Weiner Dog, which can follow this animal down its burrow. This creature is generally grey with white and black stripes on its face. Name this heavier relative of the weasel, associated with the University of Wisconsin, which is both similar to and different from the Wolverine.

He was named after an intestinal beetle that caused his mother's menstruation to be screwed up and his difficult birth and loss of his father Senzangakona caused him to be an unparalleled mama's boy. His death was no less inglorious, as he was tossed into a grain pot. In between, an Mtetwa chieftain named Dingiswayo saw potential in this man, and he rose to be chief among the Mtetwa. Among the first groups he went after were his own eLangeni clain, who had insulted him during childhood. He eventually came to occupy all of the Natal region, and is famed for unifying his tribe. FTP, name this man, the most famous chieftain of the Zulu people.

He receives beatings when he attempts to steal the clothes of some Benedictine monks, and again when his companion's horse disturbs the fillies of the Yangüesian horse-breeders. He also suffers when he drinks "the true balsam of Fierabras" prepared by his companion. He tries to convince his master that a cage is not an enchantment. He rides the donkey Dapple, and is repulsed when he learns that his friend's beloved Dulcinea is a common woman. FTP name this sidekick of Don Quixote.

His son Eumelus brought what were said to be the fastest horses at the Trojan War. With the help of Apollo, he gained his wife by yoking a lion and boar to a chariot. This because he had been a kind master when the god was made to serve him to atone for killing the Cyclops. Best known for his faithful wife, this is--for 10 points--what king of Pherae whose queen, Alcestis, agreed to die in his place only to be saved by Heracles?

After killing Sinis, he persuaded Sinis' daughter Perigune to come out of hiding by promising not to harm her. He then proceeded to rape her, producing the son Melanippus, and gave her to Deioneus as a wife. His other "heroic" deeds include killing his son Hippolytus (who was falsely accused of rape) and abandoning Ariadne on the island of Naxos after she had helped him to escape from Crete. FTP, name this hero who also killed the Minotaur.

"Death and the Compass" tells of four murders corresponding to the four letters of the name of God. "The Garden of Forking Paths" tells of a Chinese agent of the German Reich who kills an eminent Sinologist. "The Circular Ruins" portrays a magician who discovers that he is a figment of someone else's imagination. "The Library of Babel" tells of a collection of every book that could ever be written. These are among the short stories of -- FTP -- which Argentine author?

This minor goddess of Norse mythology is associated with an echoing rock near Saint Goarshausen, a place long known as a frequent site of shipwrecks. She was later said to be a brokenhearted maiden who threw herself into the Rhine River and whose ghost still seeks revenge on all males. FTP, name this subject of a Heinrich Heine poem whose voice lured sailors to their deaths.

King Oeneus forgot to mention the goddess Artemis in his annual harvest sacrifices. As punishment, Artemis sent this monster to ravage Oeneus' kingdom, which Oeneus' son fought with the help of an all-star team of hunters that included Jason, Castor, Pollux, and Theseus. FTP, name this mythical beast ultimately killed by Meleager, who awarded the trophy to Atalanta with tragic results.

She rode on a three-legged horse, and during plagues, she would depopulate entire villages by sweeping her broom-- a legend which is probably responsible for the traditional association of witches and brooms. At home, she kept court in the great hall of Elvidner, where she received perjurers, people who died of old age, and people who died without shedding blood. FTP, name this daughter of Loki and Queen of Nifelheim, the Norse goddess of death.

The ritual killing of a hippopotamus at Edfu symbolized the triumph of this god. He took the form of Harmakhis as patron of the rising sun, and in that guise his symbol was often found on amulets signifying resurrection. The "name" known as that of this god was the first royal title taken by a new Pharaoh, and the wedjat represented the eye of this god, which was partially restored, and explained the phases of the moon. The reconciliation between himself and Seth was the mythical reflection of the union of Upper and Lower Egypt. Name this god who fought Seth to avenge his father Osiris and had a falcon's head.

The same figure who was the subject of Conrad Aiken's biography Ushant was described in a T.S. Eliot poem by this name. A novel by this name includes a character who revels in sharing harsh truths, Countess Gemini, and a sickly man who leaves his estate to the protagonist so that she may escape her marriage, Ralph Touchett. Near the end, the father of Madame Merle's daughter Pansy is revealed, and the main character once more rejects the overtures of Caspar Goodwood. Name this Henry James novel in which Gilbert Osmond proves a less than ideal match for Isabel Archer.

This god was attacked by one of the avatars of Vishnu, Rama-with-an-axe. He won his wives in a contest to circumnavigate the earth with his brother; he won by travelling mentally through study while Kartikkeya trudged on foot. Those wives, who represent prudence and wisdom, are Siddhi and Buddhi. This god's mother asked Sani to look at him as a newborn, even though Sani was cursed to destroy anything he gazed upon; that, combined with his task of guarding the cave where his mother Parvati was bathing, led to his present appearance. Name this remover of obstacles who has a one-tusked elephant's head.

The "neo" form of this group was advocated by such nineteenth-century figures as Vincenzo Gioberti, who explained its revival in On the Moral and Civil Primacy of the Italians. Earlier, this group controlled the cities of Montepulciano, Orvieto, and Bologna and drew support from merchants. Its later form sympathized with Angevin control of south Italy, and this group, named after the dynasty which held the dukedom of Bavaria, was defined by its support for the Papacy against the Holy Roman Emperor. Name this faction, which in Florence was further divided into the Black and White parties, the opponents of the Ghibbelines.

One figure in this myth system was sent to the bottom of the sea to find a lost fish-hook. While on the question, he married the daughter of the god of the sea and got all the fish to help in his search. Other exciting undersea objects in this culture include the Tide Jewels, which can cause high and low tide, respectively, when thrown into the water. Some demons in this mythology have three eyes and scratch people with their fingernails, while others have the bodies of tortoises, ride flying cucumbers, and pull children into the water. In addition to the oni and the kappa, this mythology believes in an incident where a storm god annoyed his sister by throwing a flayed horse into her hall, leading to Uzume needing to lure the sun out of a cave. Name this mythology, whose chief deities include the sun goddess Amaterasu.

The son of Chysaor and the nephew of Medusa, this being lived in the far west on the island of Erytheia. He was killed for his prized possessions, which were transported to Greece and eventually sacrificed to Hera by Eurystheus, although Cacus stole some of them in transit. Orthrus, his two- headed watchdog, and Eurythion, his herdsman, were clubbed to death, and he was shot with arrows before his three bodies were ripped apart. FTP, who was this cattle owner whose herd was the object of Hercules' tenth labor?

Sometimes identified with Vili or Lodur, this god was the son of the fire giants Laufey and Farbauti [far-BOUT-ee]. Disguised as a horse, he mated with Svadilfari [sva-dill-FAR-ee], later giving birth to the 8-legged horse Sleipnir. Disguised as the witch Thokk, he was the only living creature not to weep for Baldur's death. His wife is Sigyn, though it was with the giantess Angrboda [ong-er-BOD-da] that he fathered three famous monsters. The nemesis of Heimdall is, FTP, what Norse trickster god?

On the day of his birth he stole the cattle of Apollo which, after a few angry words, he exchanged in return for the lyre which he had just invented. A son of Zeus and Maia, he was known for slaying the hundred-eyed monster Argus, and in his role as a psychopomp he escorted the dead to the underworld. Adorned with a traveler's hat and carrying the snake-entwined caduceus, FTP name this Olympian, the archetypal trickster and messenger God.

Some stories state that he came from Thessaly, and that he married Camese, who bore him the river god Tiberinus. Typically depicted with a key in his right hand, he sheltered the fleeing Saturn in Latium. During times of war the gates of his temple were left open so he could intervene if needed. The god of gates and doors, beginnings and endings, FTP name this two-faced Roman god.

Before her epic clash with the adversary who killed her, she fashioned ugallu-demons, lahmu-heroes, fish-men, and scorpion men to aid her in the fight. When her consort urged her to kill all their offspring, she refused. Later, after Apsu was killed by Enki, she sought revenge. After her death her eyes became the Tigris and Euphrates and her body the dome of heaven. Killed when Marduk crushed her head, FTP who is this ancient Near East dragon goddess?

Accompanied by Odysseus, this Argive king caught the Trojan spy Dolon and proceeded to kill Rhesus of Thrace in order to steal his horses. This son of Tydeus is injured by Pandarus in Book 5 of the Iliad, but with the aid of Athena he proceeds to single-handedly drive back the Trojans, injuring Aeneas, Aphrodite, and Ares in the process. FTP, who was this Greek hero of the Trojan war who shares his name with the owner of a set of flesh-eating mares captured in the eighth labor of Hercules?

It is thought to have been spoken by people who worshiped a patriarchal sky god and lived north of the Black Sea, then spread to Europe and Asia. Jacob Grimm noted phonetic correspondences between several languages, although Sir William Jones first noticed the similarities between Sanskrit, Greek, and Latin, thus providing evidence for this common source. FTP, name this hypothetical root language from which all Indo-European languages are descended.

Originally he was probably a god of agriculture, often identified with Silvanus. Unlike his Greek counterpart, who was a child of Zeus, his "father" was a flower that impregnated his mother, Juno. Second only to Jupiter as a patron of Rome, he was married to Nerio, but had a famous affair with Rhea Silvia. Known to the army as "Gradivus", as well as "Ultor", or avenger, FTP, name this Roman divinity, namesake of the third month, and generally identified with Ares.

Some anthropologists have speculated that this concept is the origin of some of the dietary laws prohibiting the killing of animals that appears in biblical literature. It holds that that every tribe of people evolved from separate species of animals and comes from the Ojibwa term for "brother-sister kinship." FTP, what is this belief, paired with "taboo" as the subject of a Freud work, which has been applied to the guardian spirits carved into poles by tribes in the Pacific Northwest?

After its principle owner's death, Magni and Modi will inherit it. This object was greatly feared by the frost giants, many of whom were disposed using it. Made for its owner by the dwarfs Brok and Eitri, every time it was thrown, lightning would flash and it would return to its owner's gloved hand. FTP, name this object from Norse mythology, the hammer wielded by Thor.

The owner of the staff Gambantein took a special journey to meet this figure, passing by the guard Modgud. According to some accounts, the other guards of this niece of Byleist included a giant in the form of an eagle named Hraesvelg, and a four-eyed inhabitant of the Gnipa-cave. Thokk's refusal to cry doomed Hermod's mission to procure the release of Nanna's husband from this character. Thus, she got to keep Balder in her realm in Niflheim. FTP, name this youngest child of Angrboda and Loki, the ruler and namesake of the Norse underworld.

By a coincidence, this woman's son was discovered exposed on a hillside by king Corythus's shepherds at the same time that Corythus's cattle-herders found Auge's son by Heracles. Her son later defeated the Argonaut Idas, and was one of the Seven Against Thebes. The centaurs Hylaeus and Rhaecus decided to ravish her, but she killed them and then went to stand by the side of Cleopatra's husband, who had fallen in love with her. She wound up yoked to the chariot of Cybele in the form of a lion alongside her husband Hippomenes or Melanion, who used three golden apples to distract her during a footrace. FTP, name this huntress to whom the infatuated Meleager gave the pelt of the Calydonian Boar.

In one text, this god's nose begins bleeding when he is forced to bow to a god sometimes referred to as Lord of Blood and Butchery. He was sometimes equated with Baal, leading to stories in which he defeats the sea-god Yam and rescues Astarte. He sometimes assumed the form of the bull Bata, and his son Maga was a crocodile. As the strongest god, he was invaluable in defeating Apophis. In the form of a black boar he swallowed the moon, which represented the eye of his enemy, who sometimes took the form of a falcon. FTP, name this husband of Nephthys who fought with his nephew Horus after killing his brother Osiris.

He once saved a son of Vayu by placing an iron statue in front of the blind husband of Gandhari. He was accused of murdering Prasena over the magic jewel Syamantaka, and his search for the jewel resulted in three weeks of single combat which ended with him killing the king of the bears, Jambhavan. Agni gave him a magic quoit weapon which he used to kill Sisupala, the original betrothed of this character's wife Rukmini. His older brother was born from a white hair plucked from the serpent Sesha, and he was born from a black hair plucked from Vishnu. FTP, name this avatar of Vishnu who lectures Arjuna in the Bhagavad Gita.

This figure tore out a mange-like bald patch on the chest of the Cyclops Brontes, and used some white mud to confound Alpheius. She was tricked into killing a man nicknamed Candaon, whom she met while he was trying to avenge himself on Oenopion. One of her sacred creatures, which had brazen hooves and golden stag-like horns, ran all the way to Istria and the land of the Hyperboreans during a labor of Heracles. Her devotees included Iphigenia and Hippolytus, who vowed to remain chaste like her. Immediately after being born at Ortygia, she helped her mother cross the straits to Delos, where her twin brother was born. FTP, name this twin sister of Apollo, the Greek goddess of the hunt.

Heracles rescued one of this figure's gardeners from a hole covered by a heavy stone, after which the gardener was transformed into a short-eared owl. His servants included the herdsman Menoetius and the aforementioned gardener Ascalaphus, as well as a miser who was punished for a year for giving free passage to Heracles. A son of Dia tried to kidnap his wife after helping Theseus kidnap Helen, but Pirithous ended up stuck to a chair in his palace. His wife, who carried on a part-time affair with Adonis, was a daughter of Demeter who was forced to marry him after eating some pomegranate seeds. FTP, name this Greek god of the dead.

In one branch of the Mabinogion, one of these items smeared with poison is used to kill a character sometimes known as "Pierced-Thighs." In Greek myth, scrapings from one of these items were used to heal Telephus, and in Japanese myth, Izanagi and Izanami created the first island using a jeweled one known as Amenonuhoko. Other mythical examples include Rhongomiant, one whose name meant "swaying one," and the Gae Bolga of Cuchulainn. One of these was thrown overhead to signal the start of the war of the Aesir and Vanir, and Achilles used one of these weapons to kill Hector. FTP, name this type of weapon, exemplified by Odin's Gungnir.

The Borbonicus Codex depicts him holding his turquoise fire serpent in one hand and also shows this deity holding a paper flag. His most famous temple contained several Eagle Men who perhaps represented the rising sun. He is depicted in drawings such as the Florentine Codex with feathers on his head, and he is also the god of journeys as he led his people to their adopted home. The head of his sister, which he cut off in vengeance, was tossed into the air by this deity to become the moon. The reason for this act was his mysterious conception involving a ball of feathers touching his mother Coatlicue and thus upsetting Coyolxauhqui. His name is sometimes translated to mean "Hummingbird of the Left". Known for a festival consisting of a 25 day bloody orgy of sacrifice, FTP, name this national god of the Aztecs who, along with Tlaloc, had a temple devoted to him in Tenochtitlan.

Animals sacred to this god include the gazelle and the pig, and this god is sometimes said to be the consort of a goddess who guides spirits to the Lightland. He is sometimes referred to as the "Lord of the Northern Sky" and storms and foul weather are considered under his domain. One of his functions in the underworld is taking the souls of the reckless, although he also helps out Ra in his nightly battle against Apep. He alone rejected a mediation by Neith, and this red headed god was associated with foreigners like the Hyksos, who made him the chief deity. His most famous myth involves a prolonged battle with his nephew in which this sort of aardvark headed god was castrated after gouging out the left eye of his nephew, Horus. FTP, identify this Egyptian god of deserts and chaos, the jealous killer of Osiris.

His father was most likely imprisoned in Chao at the time of his birth, contrary to some claims that he was the natural son of the man who would become his regent. This ruler's grand counsellor advised him against sending all foreigners out of his country, although he did outlaw feudalism and forced the feudal lords to move to Hsien-yang. His reliance on court magicians drew controversy from the Confucians, many of whom he subsequently executed along with staging a Burning of the Books. He linked several structures previously constructed during the Warring States period to create a version of the Great Wall that preceded the Ming version by 1600 years. Although his namesake dynasty that was supposed to last "10,000 generations" was soon eclipsed by the Han dynasty, he did leave for posterity some 8,000 terracotta soldiers surrounding his tomb. FTP, name this man who unified China and became its self-proclaimed first emperor.

The Skaldskaparmal relates how Fulla, the handmaiden of this god's grandmother, was the recipient of a ring and other gifts from this man's mother following an unsuccessful quest by Hermod. According to the Gylfaginning, he bides "the full day through" in his home, where he "puts to sleep all suits," and that home is described as pillared with gold and "with silver thatched." A resident of Glitnir, according to one legend, he led the twelve Asegir who were compiling local laws to Heligoland, and his name has evolved into the modern Icelandic word for "president." None dare break a vow made before this god, and though he was respected as the patron of all judicial assemblies, he is seldom mentioned except in connection with his father Balder. FTP, identify this Norse god of truth and justice.

An artifact found at Öland, Sweden was used to invoke this figure for protection and is known as the Kvinneby amulet. In one story, he breaks a pillar by throwing a goblet and disguises himself as a youth to get on a rowboat to catch some bait, but Hymir cuts his fishing line before he is able to unleash Sky-Bellower on his target. In another, Utgarda-Loki tricks him into wrestling with Elli, the personification of old age, before turning a certain monster into a cat and convincing this character to try to lift him. Tanngrisnir and Tanngnjostr are a pair of goats who draw this god's chariot, and he lives in the palace Bilskirnir. He is fated to take nine steps before dying from his adversary's poison after killing Jormungandr, the Midgard Serpent, at Ragnarok. FTP, name this Norse god, the owner of Megingjord, a belt which grants him strength, and Mjolnir, a war-hammer that causes lightning.

In Ojibwe mythology Nanabozho, the Great one of these is associated with the creation of the world, while the an Egyptian god with the head of one of these creatures is usually shown holding a knife in both hands and is known as Wenenut. In Aztec mythology, a group of four hundred gods of this creature called Centzon Totochtin were emblematic of fertility and drunkenness. The Japanese and Koreans believe that they make snacks out of rice while the Chinese believe that one is pounding herbs, and all three believe that these creatures do so on the moon. This creature's prevalence as a trickster figure in Central and Southern Africa probably influenced a central figure of the Uncle Remus stories. FTP, identify this four-legged Lagomorph whose foot is associated with luck.

A figure paradoxically held to be the brother of both this figure and his grandson was driven into the sea by Wichama. This being is responsible for the destructive event known as ono pacakoti, after which the world was repopulated by the offspring of Inti, his son. This god, with a name meaning "sea foam," has servants known as suncasapa, or bearded ones. Aymara tradition holds that he walked away across the Pacific Ocean after seeing the plight of Manco Capac's descendents. FTP, name this sun and storm god, the supreme deity of the Inca pantheon.

In Sudanese mythology, a son of the supreme deity Gurian Tunggal takes the form of a black one of these creatures to protect a princess. In the Popol Vuh, the half-brothers of Xbalanque and Hunapu are transformed into these creatures after getting stuck in a tree. One of these creatures always gains half the strength of his enemy in a fight and is supplanted as ruler of Kishkindha by his brother Sugriva. Another of these creatures tries to eat the sun and has his tail set on fire by Ravana. Another one of them knows the ways of seventy-two transformations and spitefully eats peaches of immortality; he is forced to repent by helping a monk obtain Buddhist scriptures in a Chinese epic. FTP, identify these creatures, examples of which include Hanuman and Journey to the West's Sun Wukong.

According to one story, Maui was killed by the vagina of Hine-nui-te-po in an attempt to make this property widespread by crushing that goddess's heart. Meghanada got this, along with a new name, by defeating Indra, while Zephyrus's horse sons Balius and Xanthus had this characteristic. Some fruit conferring this property was carried by Zhong Liquan, members of a famous group that exhibited it. Unlike her siblings, Medusa did not exhibit this property, which Cheiron bestowed upon Prometheus after being hit by an arrow. FTP, name this characteristic, which Castor was allowed to share with Pollux and which names eight characters in Daoist mythology.
